title: Orientation kit: component lifecycle guides, usage examples and migration notes
creator: Lena Ko
description: Create an "orientation kit" set of documentation pages and examples that explain recommended usage, anti-patterns, and migration steps for the tokens and key components (buttons, data tables, charts). This ticket covers content design, example code snippets, migration checklist, and a small set of live examples for the docs site. The goal is to reduce developer confusion, lower migration effort for product teams, and reduce support tickets caused by breaking token/prop changes.
acceptance_criteria: A1: New docs pages for Tokens, Buttons, Tables, and Charts exist on the docs site under /guides/orientation-kit
A2: Each page includes: recommended API surface, 3 real-world examples, 3 'Do' and 'Don't' items, accessibility notes, and a migration checklist
A3: Migration checklist contains step-by-step mapping from legacy token names to new token scale plus a scripted helper (link to GH) and automated smoke tests
A4: Design Review approval recorded and at least two cross-functional reviewers have signed off
A5: Frontend engineering has confirmed examples compile in the docs playground and the CI job passes
A6: Metrics: initial docs page views and a baseline for "migration support tickets" are captured in the rollout dashboard
tasks: Audit current token usage across component examples and internal templates (DES and ENG to collaborate)
Draft user-focused 'orientation' narratives for tokens and each component: why this API, when to use variants
Author three canonical examples for each component: Minimal, Real Product Case, Edge Case
Produce explicit Do/Don't rows for each component with short rationale and code snippets
Write migration mapping table for legacy tokens -> new tokens and include quick copy/paste CSSVars snippet
Create a tiny migration script (node) that rewrites token keys in CSS/SCSS files; open GH PR
Add accessibility notes (keyboard patterns, ARIA guidance, color contrast checks) and link to QA checklist
Coordinate with Docs Ops to add pages, embed live runnable examples, and add smoke tests to CI
Collect signoffs from PM, Engineering, and DevRel and publish final pages
discussion: 2026-02-16: Tomás Ruiz (ENG) — recommended limiting breaking prop renames to only tokens; suggested aliasing old props for one release cycle
2026-02-20: Marcus Singh (PM) — wants migration checklist prioritized; flagged two enterprise customers on legacy token set
2026-02-24: Design sync — propose 'orientation kit' as a single landing page that branches to the four focused guides
2026-02-28: Aisha — suggested adding a 'quick revert' pattern for teams that hit regressions during rollout
2026-03-03: Engineering review notes — ensure examples use the runtime-safe import paths and avoid internal experimental props
2026-03-07: UX Research — proposed adding a short micro-survey on the docs pages to capture friction points
decisions: Ship docs as an 'orientation kit' landing page with tokens, buttons, tables, charts as subsections
Provide one release-cycle compatibility layer: shim CSS Vars plus a deprecation note on legacy token pages
Do not change chart public props in this release; only update docs to guide usage for the new color/token scheme
Include runnable React + TS examples and a CodeSandbox template for each component
Add a migration script in GH repo `redwood/design-tools` and tag ENG for maintenance
notes: Implementation should emphasize minimal churn for integrators. Keep code examples idiomatic (React + TypeScript) and provide plain JS/CSS fallbacks. The migration script is intentionally conservative: it only renames tokens in CSS custom properties and creates a backup. Follow-up ticket will track removal of shims after one release cycle. Track support ticket volume for 6 weeks post-release to validate impact. QA owners: ENG-frontend team; Docs Ops will maintain the runnable sandbox templates.
